title: Audit scrapheap: SOC2 triage + evidence heuristics (personal)
content:
Context / purpose:
Quick brain dump for myself: what I need to triage first for our SOC2 readiness run. This is messy — notes to self, heuristics for evidence hunting, and short checklists I can hand off to Ellie or Maya. Not for sharing externally yet.

High-level goals (short):
- Identify low-effort, high-impact evidence we can collect in 2 weeks.
- Make a prioritized backlog of controls that are most likely to block the audit (access, change control, logging).
- Create simple queries and locations where evidence likely lives (s3 buckets, cloud logs, console screenshots).

Quick wins (target 10–14 days):
1) Access reviews: export IAM role lists, last-used timestamps, and confirm 2 admins removed (task: run iam-last-used report).
2) MFA rollout: produce screenshot + link to policy page + short guide for auditors showing enforcement (ok if staged).
3) Backup policy + recent snapshot evidence: S3 snapshots for dbs and a retention table (timestamped).
4) Incident notification proof: one Pager showing pager duty rotation + example incident ticket (redact PII).

Top risk areas (my gut):
- Privileged access sprawl on dedicated infra (private deployments) — we need explicit owner for each reserved-cluster.
- Inconsistent config drift for on-prem package (customer-specific deploys) — evidence of automated config checks is weak.
- Logging retention gaps: some metrics/logs older than 90 days archived offsite with no easy retrieval.

Evidence hunting heuristics (how I look for stuff):
- Start with people: who touched the component in last 6 months (PR history, CloudTrail, git blame).
- Follow the pipeline: codecommit -> CI job -> infra deploy -> running instance. Evidence often lives at the CI job output (artifact + deployed tag).
- If a thing is "manual" (eg ad-hoc DB export), look for slack threads around the timestamp and payroll tickets.

Useful quick queries / commands (copyable):
- AWS: aws iam get-service-last-accessed --arn <role_arn> (or list-access-keys with last-used)
- GCP: gcloud projects get-iam-policy <proj> --format json > policy.json
- Logging: elasticsearch/_search?q=service:ingest AND @timestamp:[now-90d TO now]
- Git history: git log --since="2025-09-01" --pretty=format:'%h %an %s' infra/cluster-configs

Control mapping shortcuts (very rough):
- Access controls (CC1): IAM roles + periodic review notes + MFA enforcement screenshot
- Change management (CC2): PRs with approvals + CI pass + release tag + canary rollout dashboard screenshot
- Logging & monitoring (CC3): CloudTrail/Stackdriver sample, retention policy doc, alert routing to PD
- Vendor mgmt (CC4): list of third-party libs and a recent license scan (Snyk/OSS check)

Questions for auditors / unresolved items to clarify:
- Do auditors accept redacted production tickets as evidence, or do they need native logs? (ask Ellie)
- When they ask for evidence of key rotation, do they want KMS rotation policy or actual rotation records?
- How deep do they go on private deployments that are customer-managed? (scope clarification)

Evidence packaging notes (how I plan to present):
- One control = 1 folder with: policy doc (pdf), annotated screenshot(s), 1–2 raw artifacts (log snippet/PR link), a short narrative (2–3 bullets) describing why this proves the control.
- Use consistent filenames: control-<id>_-_<artifact-type>_YYYYMMDD (makes mapping easy).

Owner matrix (initial):
- Access reviews -> Maya (run IAM and compile list)
- Logging retention -> Ellie (validate S3/glacier retrieval + make retention table)
- Change mgmt evidence -> me (Pranav) (collect PRs and canary dashboard shots)

Mini-runbook for evidence redaction (notes):
- Remove customer names/ids, replace with CUSTOMER-001 tokens.
- For logs: include only the minimal fields auditors need (timestamp, actor, action, resource).
- Keep raw evidence archived in a read-only bucket with an index file linking redacted ↔ raw (raw only for auditors with NDA).

What to avoid (common traps):
- Hand-scraped screenshots without metadata (no timestamp or URL). Auditors ask for where it came from.
- Mixing docs from different dates with no versioning — add a small header in each artifact showing collected_at and collector name.

Communication plan (for the team):
- Quick sync Wed 10am (15m) to assign first-pass backlog.
- Drop a single thread in #trust-ops called "soc2-evidence-pack-YYYYMM" with ongoing status updates.

Tasks / TODOs (immediate):
- [ ] Run iam-last-used and share csv (Maya) — due 2026-02-22
- [ ] Snapshot of canary rollout dashboard + steps to reproduce (Pranav) — due 2026-02-24
- [ ] Inventory of all KMS keys + rotation policy doc (Ellie) — due 2026-02-26
- [ ] Draft control folder template (me) — due 2026-02-20 (blocking)

Random scribbles (notes to self):
- consider a small script to pull PR approvals + approver emails to create a compact change control export
- check marketplace billing for any third-party tools that need vendor evidence (Sentry/Datadog)
- for private deployment customers, flag which ones run older infra (k8s 1.24) — auditors care about known-vuln timelines

Last thought: keep the first evidence pass focused on reproducible artifacts (PRs, CI logs, policy pages). Live system logs harder but we can scope them later. If we get the quick wins, auditors will usually let us iterate on the rest.

---
End of scrapheap. Will tidy into a proper control mapping doc once we have CSVs from Maya and the KMS inventory from Ellie.
